payload.headline: Deep mutual attraction and high maturity cannot overcome a declared, absolute contradiction about having children.
payload.rationale: Strengths: Both describe strong mutual warmth, secure attachment, and high emotional maturity—ingredients that typically support honest communication, gentle boundaries, and amiable parting if needed. Live tension: Tom has explicitly and non-negotiably stated he will never have children; Lena has explicitly and non-negotiably stated she wants three children and will not partner with someone who refuses parenthood. This is a declared dealbreaker contradiction on a core life purpose axis (family/parenting), not an inferred or repairable pattern. Character modulation: their maturity and growth orientation lower the risk of coercion, concealment, or acrimony; they are likely to handle a breakup with respect rather than harm. But maturity cannot transform mutually exclusive, identity-defining life goals into a shared future. What would have to change: one party would need to revise an explicit, absolute life goal (Tom accepting children or Lena relinquishing motherhood as central)—a realistic possibility only if one genuinely re-evaluates core priorities, which both currently state as non-negotiable. Given the explicit declarations, the ethical and practical decision is not_a_match despite clear attraction.
open_tensions: Very strong mutual attraction and secure attachment—chemistry is real
Explicit, absolute contradiction on children (declared dealbreakers) — core, identity-defining
High emotional maturity reduces risk of harm but does not resolve the core incompatibility
Resolution would require one party to change a declared non-negotiable (unlikely)
A graceful, amicable separation is likely if pursued honestly
